lead.tldr: Tether fundraising delay risk indicates liquidity strain for stablecoin issuers, could affect market confidence • Institutional entry expands as Charles Schwab launches spot Bitcoin/Ethereum trading, accelerating retail exposure • IMF warning on tokenised finance heightens regulatory scrutiny, founders must embed compliance early to mitigate systemic risk • Bitcoin whales losing $337 million daily in Q1 signals sustained downtrend, raising margin call concerns for large holders • Spot Bitcoin ETF inflows outpace gold, supporting analyst view that crypto ETFs could surpass traditional asset funds

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, Tether’s $500 billion valuation round may stall if demand wanes, while the IMF warns tokenised finance could outpace oversight, and Charles Schwab’s new crypto brokerage underscores growing institutional appetite. Meanwhile, Bitcoin ETFs are poised to eclipse gold funds as capital shifts.

top_signals.title: Tether May Delay Fundraising If Demand Falls Short at $500B Valuation
top_signals.summary: Tether disclosed that it intends to launch a new fundraising round that would place the stablecoin issuer at a $500 billion valuation. The company cautioned that insufficient investor demand could force a postponement of the round. This signals heightened capital requirements for Tether as it navigates persistent market volatility and regulatory scrutiny, a factor that institutional investors should monitor.

top_signals.title: Crypto startups raised $5 billion in Q1 — here are the top 10 funding rounds
top_signals.summary: Crypto startups raised roughly $5 billion in Q1 2026, representing a 16% decline from the prior year but still indicating robust investor appetite. The largest share of capital went to prediction‑market platforms which secured about $1.7 billion, while payments and trading‑infrastructure firms captured the next biggest portions. Among the ten biggest rounds Kalshi attracted $1 billion and Polymarket raised $600 million, underscoring continued institutional focus on high‑growth verticals within the crypto ecosystem.

top_signals.title: Tokenised finance is a double-edged sword without proper oversight, IMF warns
top_signals.summary: The International Monetary Fund has warned that the rapid tokenisation of financial assets could increase systemic risk when oversight and policy frameworks are insufficient. It notes that faster settlement and automated market structures may compress the window for regulatory intervention during periods of stress. Major Wall Street participants including BlackRock, JP Morgan and the New York Stock Exchange are actively pursuing tokenised securities offerings. Institutional investors should monitor the development of regulatory safeguards as the speed of tokenised transactions grows.

top_signals.title: Charles Schwab to debut Bitcoin and Ethereum trading
top_signals.summary: Charles Schwab is launching a new brokerage product called Schwab Crypto that will enable customers to trade Bitcoin and Ethereum on a spot basis. The offering adds direct exposure to the two largest digital assets within Schwab’s existing platform. This launch follows a broader wave of Wall Street firms expanding crypto services and reflects growing institutional acceptance of digital assets.

top_signals.title: Bitcoin Whales, Sharks Realized $337M in Daily Losses in Q1 2026
top_signals.summary: On-chain analysis indicates that large Bitcoin holders, often referred to as whales, experienced an average daily loss of $337 million in Q1 2026. This loss reflects a steep drawdown in Bitcoin prices during the period. The sustained price pressure increases portfolio risk for high‑net‑worth investors and may affect liquidity in the broader crypto market. Institutional investors should monitor whale activity as a leading indicator of market sentiment.

top_signals.title: Polymarket Pulls Missing US Pilot Market, Faces Questions Over Rules
top_signals.summary: Polymarket, a decentralized prediction‑market platform, has withdrawn its US pilot offering. The decision follows backlash and scrutiny over the platform’s rule set. The move highlights growing regulatory pressure on crypto‑based prediction markets and signals caution for institutional investors.

top_signals.title: Bitcoin ETFs Will Be Bigger Than Gold ETFs, Says ETF Analyst
top_signals.summary: James Seyffart, an ETF analyst, says Bitcoin exchange‑traded funds are on track to surpass gold ETFs in assets under management. He points to the rapid inflows that have followed the introduction of spot Bitcoin ETFs as evidence of growing demand. The projection signals a broader reallocation of capital from traditional safe‑haven products to crypto‑focused investment vehicles, a trend that institutional investors should monitor.

top_signals.title: Ethereum Foundation Less Than 500 ETH Away From Hitting 70K Staked ETH Goal
top_signals.summary: The Ethereum Foundation announced that it is now less than 500 ETH away from reaching its target of 70,000 ETH staked on the network. Achieving the 70,000 ETH stake level would demonstrate robust participation from validators. A higher stake volume is expected to further secure the Ethereum proof‑of‑stake chain.

linkedin_post: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, The crypto landscape continues to evolve at a rapid pace and the signals we see this quarter are worth a close look. Tether has announced a plan to launch a new fundraising round that would value the stablecoin issuer at $500 billion. The company warned that if investor demand falls short the round could be delayed, a reminder that even the biggest players must navigate market volatility and regulatory scrutiny. For institutional investors this is a cue to watch capital flows and risk appetite closely. At the same time crypto startups raised roughly $5 billion in the first quarter of 2026. While that represents a modest dip from last year, the capital still flowed strongly into high‑growth verticals. Prediction‑market platforms captured the lion’s share with $1.7 billion, led by Kalshi’s $1 billion round and Polymarket’s $600 million raise. Payments and trading‑infrastructure firms followed, highlighting where investors see durable value creation. The International Monetary Fund has issued a cautionary note on tokenised finance. It warns that rapid tokenisation of assets can raise systemic risk when oversight is thin. Faster settlement and automated market structures may shrink the window for regulators to act during stress. With Wall Street giants such as BlackRock, JP Morgan and the NYSE moving into tokenised securities, the need for robust policy frameworks has never been clearer.
